item.title: Re: My Thoughts
item.content:encoded: Thanks so much for the advice! It’s all implemented! I would like to throw out the idea that it is actually completely possible this guy’s got a script memorized for situations like these, or at least has parts of this prepared beforehand. It’s supposed to be a one-sided sort of deal, more of an argument to join his side rather than some natural conversation.

item.title: My Thoughts
item.content:encoded:
Reading this, I feel like the characters are reading off of a story or script rather than having more of a natural conversation (unless that one speaker is really extra). I am a bit mindful that this is a conversation, so of course it shouldn't be perfect since people in-universe make mistakes too, and given the circumstance they're in.

+ Here are my thoughts
- More like crit...

What actually happened was an eleven-foot tall mammal-like reptile you might call a “chupacabra”

I feel like you could add ", which" between the "reptile" and the "you", and maybe another comma after "chupacabra".

injected your neighbors and family with a powerful hemorrhagic poison, and then sucked up their insides

For better flow, I suggest something like, "injected a powerful hemorrhagic poison into your neighbors and family, then sucked up their insides"
That way, it sounds less awkward, and you won't have the ", and" without a subject.

That’s Special Containment Procedures.

I feel like this comes off as a bit awkward in the paragraph. How about "That stands for Special Containment Procedures." instead?

We do three things: we secure the things that go bump in the night like chupacabra back there.

I feel like you could replace the second "thing" with "anomalies", so you wouldn't have an awkward repeat of "things". Additionally, I feel like the second "we" is also unnecessary because you've already previously mentioned it. I also think there could be a comma between "night" and "like".

We contain them so things like this don’t happen.

There should probably be a comma before "so" since it's a fanboy, and the sentences on both sides could stand on their own.

You may not have looked into the void but it’s looked back at you.

What you currently have is, "… it is looked back at you". I would suggest, "… into the void, but it had looked back at you".

we fix your little fishbowl and you can go back to living in it.

Comma between "fishbowl" and "and" since it's another fanboy.

Or you don’t. That’s the other option.

I think you could rephrase it as "If you don't, that's the other option".

Not a single day is boring, though.

I personally don't see the comma as nessary, but yes, it's dialogue. Dialogue tends to be more wishy washy with grammar rules.

“Yesterday I worked with a Tibetan monk who moves at 200 kilometers per hour all day.

Feel like this could be rephrased as "All day yesterday, I worked with a Tibetan monk who moves at 200 kilometers per hour.


I know that it doesn't need to look perfect for it to be natural—especially for dialogue, but I hope this is somewhat helpful with some of the grammar. Overall, it's okay to me, but I feel like it's not enough for me to upvote. For now, it'll be a novote.

item.title: Re: A Critique
item.content:encoded: Thanks for going out of your way for that in-depth critique! I really appreciate it. Personally, I kind of prefer the flow on that second-to-last section so I think I might keep that for the time being. But this is much appreciated so thanks again!

item.title: A Critique
item.content:encoded:
Crit is somewhat out of order so be wary. I enjoyed the beginning quite a lot! +1 from me!

[+] Reveal a madman's thoughts [+]
 [-] Return to the darkness [-]

Overall, let me just say that I really enjoy this piece. I think that this serves as an excellent way to introduce new readers to the Foundation and as a good in-universe execution of an orientation.

This is a basic amnestic inhalant. Take it, and we fix your little fishbowl and you can go back to living in it. Or you don’t. That’s the other option. Remember it all. Maybe you’re sick of the fishbowl. 

I especially liked the red pill, blue pill scenario toward the end. If you drew inspiration from the Matrix (which is where my mind immediately went), then this is a neat little Easter egg. Correlatively I think this is a good analogy for what joining the Foundation is like. Maybe it would he better for some to live in ignorance of the anomalous, maybe some want to be red pulled and wake up. I think this is interesting.

 Welcome to the real world. In every shadow is a new unspeakable monstrosity. A new hexed object. In every crowd is a human with extraordinary and terrible powers. And on every block of every street is a new shadowy organization trying to control them and you.”

This is good but there are a few things here I don't like. I feel the use of the word "In" in the second line is unnecessary. (Welcome to the real world. Every shadow…). Also a common should be added here -》(every shadow is a new, unspeakable monstrosity.). The sentences surrounding "A new hexed object" seem flavorful, but that one sentence seems rather mundane by comparison. Also, just a thing I learned in college is to avoid using the same noun or verb twice per paragraph. ("Every shadow… a new shadowy organization). For me, this breaks up the flow and takes the reader back into an earlier part of the paragraph.

“Don’t worry, we’re the good guys. And why am I saying that? Because we let you live this far. The others wouldn’t do that. You’re just gonna have to trust me on that.”

"And why am I saying that?" Seems unneeded. So, with my edit it should read "…good guys. We let you live; the others wouldn't do that.". Also the final "on that" is not needed either.

“Who are we? We are called the SCP Foundation. That’s Special Containment Procedures. We do three things: secure, contain and protect. We secure the things that go bump in the night like chupacabra back there. We contain them so things like this don’t happen. And we do it to protect you. We’re a worldwide organization comprised of scientists and agents who have dedicated our lives to this cause.”

Ah, this is nice. Just a minor thing here. "We are the SCP Foundation" instead of "We are called the SCP Foundation." The way this is written implies that the Foundation was given the name by some force other than themselves. Structurally this is sound but I think it could better. "We do three things: We secure the things that go bump in the night like chupacabra back there. We contain them so things like this don’t happen, and we do it to protect you. We’re a worldwide organization…" this is what I would change this paragraph to.

item.title: Nice
item.content:encoded: I was actually working on a dnd campaign that takes place in the scp universe, this is a perfect introductory speech to the players, also, otherwise pretty dope!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
We are called the SCP Foundation. That’s Special Containment Procedures.

It feels a bit awkward to me when people in-universe explicitly say "We are called the Special Containment Procedures Foundation" or the like. I guess being called "just The Foundation" or "The SCP Foundation (don't ask what SCP stands for)" may also be a bit odd when you think about it, but at least in a way where it isn't stated out loud.

Aside from that; I do dig little Tales like this, and it was pretty well done here. +1
